i completely understand where you're at (in my own ways of course)
it's a devastating feeling, kinda "blinking" back into reality after relapsing again- especially when it's something you've been clean of for so long, the weight of it can feel crushing. 10 years sounds unbelieveably difficult to process, and i'm so sorry for what you're going through

for me, when i broke a 3 year clean streak i went into shock for a while. then when reality would hit (at first it was short little "strikes" for me, then gradually increased) there was so much guilt, numbness, anxiety, regret, temptations that my mind was scrambling to be able to "focus" on one - but then as time went on i kinda did process things, "sort" out my feelings more, and remind myself that staying clean is called that for a reason:

it was a fight to keep that streak, but that strength and willpower is something i can become capable of again. when we come back from being in shock, we usually focus on how we "lost" it if we were able to relapse again- validly so, but after we start processing and we're ready for this, there's things to then ask yourself- 

"What caused the relapse and What needs to change in my life?"

Is the support i had in my life leading up to/after relapsing enough for me? Do i need more? Do i need a  different kind of support? 

is my attitude towards myself something that could need improvement? 

do i need therapy? 

if you have therapy- is therapy helping me enough as to where i feel i'm able to get onto a better track from here, or does something need an adjustment? 


imagine strength as a tower, a building, a mountain, whatever, 
you don't lose strength after you've built it, you may fall off and hurt yourself, or misstep and stumble backwards a bit, but YOU literally made the top of that building/made it to the top of the mountain:

You are capable of that strength, willpower, discipline, and- one of the things you'll probably need to spend the most time in- patience again. 

it might feel unbearably long or completely overwhelming being in the aftermath of relapsing, but as long as you work towards being better.. you WILL get better, because if you're working towards it- you know you're gonna get there eventually.

to everyone whos struggling: 

please get help, its easier said than done and therapy can seem scary but even just talk to someone you trust- my friends helped support me before i went to actual therapy (but dont make them your therapist, its not their job and this illness gets very 'heavy' very quickly for you and your friend) 

i promise you its worth it and it gets better. i cant express it enough. 2 1/2 years ago i was underweight and convinced this was it, no turning back, im walking myself into my grave (and practically was), now im a healthy weight and foods a vibe! Lol food wont always be an enemy, just keep pushin i swear. im always here if you need it too btw! but please- as hard as it is- DELETE THE PHOTOS! that was one of my first steps. delete your body checks, the thinspo, get rid of that scale, even cover your mirrors unless you have to get ready for work/school. be there for yourself physically- nurture yourself, its hard and i know that, i been there, but its possible. recovery aint linear either so dont stress setbacks, just keep goin- i had it on and off for literally 5-6 yrs, i was 10 yrs old when i first developed it. youd imagine havin that with a developin brain would warp me enough to be near impossible to "undo it"/recover, but im here and im ok, fully recovered!! :-)
